profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility DFW29, at 950 East Collins Boulevard, Richardson, TX 75081. Digital Realty's own property listing for DFW29, fetched this session, lists the building at 121,500 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Dallas-Fort Worth metro portfolio, concentrated in Richardson's Telecom Corridor along East Collins Boulevard, Alma Road, Security Row, and Quality Way, with additional sites elsewhere in Dallas County. Digital Realty's own Dallas metro page, fetched this session, lists numerous named properties across this footprint. Dallas-Fort Worth is one of the largest data center markets in the US, also hosting large AWS, CyrusOne, and QTS campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry; Oncor Electric Delivery is the principal utility serving most of the metro and has flagged large-load data center interconnection requests as a fast-growing category on its system. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual Dallas-area buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty markets its Dallas properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Silicon Valley, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform.

profile.regional_context: Dallas-Fort Worth is among the largest data center markets in the United States, with Richardson's Telecom Corridor and the broader metro hosting large colocation, hyperscale, and enterprise campuses for Digital Realty, CyrusOne, QTS, AWS, and other operators tracked in this registry. Oncor Electric Delivery serves most of the DFW area's transmission and distribution and has reported rapidly growing large-load interconnection requests from data centers, a trend Texas lawmakers and ERCOT have responded to with new large-load interconnection rules in recent legislative sessions. Texas offers local Chapter 380/381 economic development agreements that DFW-area municipalities have used to attract large data center investment.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's DFW29 facility in Richardson publishes 100,000 square feet of technical space but no power capacity in megawatts, making it impossible to assess its role in AI infrastructure scaling.

Without a megawatt figure, no estimate of rack density, GPU capacity, or AI workload potential can be derived from published sources. The facility holds three certifications—PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and ISO 9001—that qualify it for payment processing, information security, and quality management work respectively. None of these certifications is specific to AI, and none implies the power densities that large-scale model training or inference requires.

DFW29 occupies a meaningful footprint within Texas's recognized data center concentration, but its absence from the state's set of facilities with published power figures leaves it outside the ranking that tracks compute capacity. A 100,000-square-foot building is substantial, yet without knowing its actual power draw, its tenancy, or its workload, it cannot be placed on the scaling curve that determines whether it contributes to AI's binding constraint on the power grid. The data covers what is published, not what exists behind the facility's walls.
